The Lord himself created her. He saw her, counted her, and poured her out upon all his works.
She is with all flesh according to how he gives her, and he gave her to those who love him.

For the Lord is compassionate and merciful. He forgives sins and saves in times of distress.
Woe to a weak heart and idle hands, and to a sinner who walks on two paths!
Woe to a weak heart, because it does not trust! Therefore it will not be protected.
Woe to you who have given up endurance! What will you do when the Lord comes to examine you?
Those who fear the Lord do not disobey his words, and those who love him keep his ways.
Those who fear the Lord seek what pleases him, and those who love him seek his law.
Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts and humble their souls before him.
We will fall into the hands of the Lord, not into human hands, for his mercy is as great as his greatness.
Listen to me, my children, to your father, and act this way so that you may live.
For the Lord has honored the father above the children and established the mother's authority over her daughters.

Do not let him investigate what is beyond your affairs, for you have been taught more than human wisdom.
For many have been led astray by the thoughts within them, and their evil thoughts have made their hearts stumble.
The one who loves danger will fall into it. A stubborn heart will suffer hardship in the end.

Do not grieve a hungry soul. Do not cause a person anguish in his poverty.
Do not trouble a heart in anguish. Do not delay giving to someone in need.
Do not abandon someone who pleads with you in distress. Do not turn your face away from a poor person.
Do not turn your eyes away from someone in need. Do not give a person a reason to curse you.
For if he curses you in the anguish of his soul, the one who made him will hear his plea.
Make yourself loved in your congregation, and bow your head before your superior.
Turn your ear toward a poor person, and answer him with peaceful words and gentleness.
Rescue the person who is being oppressed from the hand of his oppressor. Do not be fainthearted when passing judgment.
Be like a father to orphans, and take the place of a husband to their mother, so that you may become a son of the Most High and your mother may love you even more.
Wisdom has exalted her children, and she welcomes those who seek her.
Whoever loves her loves life, and those who seek her early will be filled with joy.
Whoever holds firmly to her will inherit glory, and the Lord blesses the place she enters.
Those who serve her will serve the Holy One, and the Lord loves those who love her.
Whoever listens to her will judge the nations. Whoever trusts her will live securely.
If you believe, you will inherit her, and his descendants will live in a secure place.
At first she will test him by crooked ways. She will bring fear and weakness upon him and torment him with her discipline until she trusts his soul. She will test him with her requirements.
And she will turn back to him by a straight path, make him glad, and reveal her secrets to him.
If he goes astray, she will abandon him and hand him over to his downfall.
Pay attention to the time, guard yourself against evil, and do not be ashamed of your ignorance.
For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that is glory and grace.
Do not show favoritism to the harm of your soul, and do not be ashamed at your downfall.
Do not hold back a word at a time of deliverance.
For wisdom is recognized through speech, and instruction through the words of the tongue.
Do not oppose the truth, and be ashamed of your ignorance.
Do not be ashamed to confess your sins. Do not hold back a flowing river.
Do not prostrate yourself before a foolish person. Do not show favoritism to a powerful person.
Fight for the truth until death, for the Lord God fights for you.
Do not be quick to speak while being sluggish and careless in your actions.
Do not act like a lion in your house, being harsh with your servants.
Do not let your hand be stretched out to receive and then draw it back when you are about to give.
Do not put your trust in your wealth. Do not say, “It is enough for me to live on.”
Do not follow your heart and your strength <so that you walk according to the desires of your heart>.
Do not say, “Who can overpower me?” so that you follow the desires of your heart, for the Lord will surely punish you.
Do not say, “I sinned, and what happened to me?” For the Lord is patient.
Do not be fearless because forgiveness will come, and add sin to your sins.
Do not say, “His mercy is great, and he will forgive my many sins.” For mercy and wrath are in his hands, and his anger will come upon sinners.
Do not delay turning to the Lord. Do not put it off from one day to the next, for the Lord’s wrath will come suddenly, and you will perish at the time of punishment.
Do not put your trust in wealth gained unjustly, for it will not benefit you at all on the day of distress.
Do not winnow with every wind. Do not walk on every road.
Be firm in your understanding, and let your word remain consistent.
Be quick to listen, and speak your words patiently.
If you are wise, speak to your neighbor. Otherwise, put your hand over your mouth.
For honor and disgrace are in speech, and a person’s tongue is his downfall.
Do not let yourself be called a slanderer, and do not let yourself be trapped by your tongue. For a thief has shame, and a two-tongued person has an evil accusation against him.

Do not be ignorant in matters great or small. (Chapter 6, verse 1) Instead of becoming a friend, do not become an enemy, for a bad name will inherit shame and reproach. Such is the two-tongued sinner.
(Compare chapter 5, verse 15.)
Do not exalt yourself in the counsel of your heart, lest they tear your soul apart like a calf.
They will eat your branches, and you will destroy your fruit and leave yourself like dry trees.
An evil soul destroys the person who harbors it and makes his enemies rejoice over him.
An eloquent tongue increases the number of those who call out before it.
Be at peace with everyone, but let your advisers be one in a thousand.
If you make a friend for yourself, make him your friend through your trials, and do not trust him too quickly.
For there is a friend who is only a friend for a time, and he will not remain [?] in your distress.

A faithful friend is a secure shelter; whoever finds one has found a treasure.
A faithful friend has no substitute, and his value cannot be measured.
A faithful friend is life-giving medicine; those who fear the Lord will find one.
Those who fear the Lord keep their friendship true, for as a person is, so is the one beside him.
My son, choose instruction from your youth, so that you may find favor into your old age.
Approach her like someone who plows and sows, and wait for her good fruits. You will endure a little hardship in working for her, and you will soon eat her produce.
She is like very difficult tasks to the foolish, and an uneducated person does not remain with her.

Approach her with all your strength, and keep to her paths with all your might.
Search and seek, and she will reveal herself to you. Take hold of her and do not let her go.
For in the end you will find her rest, and she will turn into joy for you.
Then those fetters will become a strong shelter for you, and those chains a glorious robe.
What she wears is a golden ornament, and her bonds are cords of blue cloth.

Do not do evil, and no evil will overtake you.

Fear the Lord with all your soul, and honor his priests.

Fear the Lord and honor his priests. Give him his due, as he commanded you: the firstfruits, the sin offering, the shoulder portion, the sacrifice of purification, and the firstfruits of the holy offerings.
Stretch out your hand to the poor, so that your blessing may be complete.
Kindness and honor in the presence of everyone; do not withhold kindness from a dead person.
Weep with those who weep, and mourn with those who mourn.
Do not hesitate to visit the sick, for they will love you for this.
In all your words, remember your end, and you will never sin.
Do not fight with a powerful person, lest you fall into his hands.
Do not contend with a rich person, lest he weigh out gold against you. For gold has ruined many and turned the hearts of kings.
Do not fight with a loudmouthed person, and do not add wood to his fire.
Do not laugh with an ignorant person, lest your parents be insulted.
Do not reproach a person who has turned away from sin. Remember that we are all subject to reproach.
Do not mock a person in his old age, for some of us grow old.
Do not rejoice over someone who has died. Remember that we will all die.
Do not neglect the words of the wise, but live by their proverbs, for through them you will learn instruction and how to serve important people.
Do not abandon the words of the elders, which they themselves were taught by their fathers, for through them you will learn wisdom, and in their time of need [?].
Do not kindle the coals of a sinner, lest you be burned in the fire of his flame.
Do not stand up against a sinner, so that he does not sit like a trap at your mouth.
Do not lend to someone more powerful than you. If you do lend, consider the money lost.
Do not guarantee a debt beyond your means. If you do guarantee it, take care to pay it.
Do not go to court against a judge, for he will be judged according to his status.
Do not travel on the road with a reckless person, so that he does not rise up against you. For he goes his own way, and you will perish through your foolishness.
Do not fight with an angry person, and do not travel with him in the wilderness. For your blood means nothing to him, and he will strike you down in a place where there is no help.
Do not consult with a fool, for they cannot keep what is said to themselves.
Do not do something secret in the presence of a stranger, for you do not know what you will do.
Do not open your heart to everyone, and do not put yourself under an obligation.
Do not be jealous of your wife, and do not teach her an evil lesson against yourself.
Do not give your heart to your wife and let her gain power over you.
Do not associate with a prostitute, lest you fall into her traps.
Do not draw near to a female singer, lest you be ruined by her activities.
Do not gaze at a virgin, lest her beauty cause you to stumble.
Do not give your heart to prostitutes, so that you do not destroy your inheritance.
Do not wander through the streets of a city or roam through its deserted places.
Turn your eyes away from a beautiful woman, and do not examine beauty that does not belong to you. Many have been led astray by the beauty of women, and through this intimacy flares up like a fire.
Never sit beside a married woman, and do not join her in drinking wine, lest your heart incline toward her and you slide into destruction in your spirit.
Do not abandon an old friend, for a new one is not equal to him. A new friend is like new wine: when it has aged, you drink it with pleasure.
Do not envy a sinner's glory, for you do not know what his downfall will be.
Do not desire what the ungodly desire. Remember that they will not be vindicated, even down to the underworld.

Keep away from a person who has the authority to kill, and you will not think about the fear of death. Even if you approach him, do not offend him, so that he does not take your life. Understand that you are walking among traps and on the walls of a city.
To the best of your ability, pay attention to yourself and your neighbor, and seek advice from wise people.
Take counsel with wise people, and let all your words concern the law of the Most High.
Let righteous people be your companions in eating and drinking, and let your boasting be in the fear of the Lord.
Work is honored through the hand of the craftsman, and the leader of a people is wise in his speech.
A loudmouthed person inspires fear in his city, and someone rash in speech is hated.
A wise judge instructs his people, and the rule of a wise person will be orderly.
As the judge of a people is, so are those who serve him. As the leader of a city is, so is everyone who lives in it.
An uneducated king leads his people astray, but a city is established through the understanding of a powerful man.
Authority over the earth is in the Lord's hand, and at the right time he raises up a suitable person over it.
A person's success is in the Lord's hand, and he bestows his glory on a scribe.
Do not be angry with your neighbor over any wrongdoing, and do not do anything arrogantly.
Pride is hated by the Lord and by people, and in the eyes of both it commits injustice.
A kingdom is transferred from one nation to another because of injustice, insults, and money.
Why do earth and ashes boast? For [?] throws out his insides while he is still alive.
A doctor watches for a severe illness, and the one who is king today will die tomorrow.
For when a person dies, reptiles, wild animals, and worms will inherit him.
The beginning of pride is when a person turns away from the Lord and his heart turns away from the one who made him.
For the beginning of pride is sin, and whoever clings to it will pour out abominations. Because of this, the Lord made his afflictions astonishing and destroyed them completely.
The Lord demolished the thrones of rulers and seated gentle people in their place.
The Lord uprooted the roots of nations and planted the humble in their place.
The Lord demolished the lands of nations and destroyed them down to the foundations of the earth.
He made some of them dry up, destroying them, and removed their memory from the earth.
Pride was not created for human beings, nor furious anger for those born of women.

What offspring are honored? Human offspring. What offspring are honored? Those who fear the Lord. What offspring are despised? Human offspring. The offspring who are despised are those who break the commandments.
The one honored among brothers is their leader, and those who fear the Lord are honored in his presence.
A convert, a rich person, a foreigner, an honored person, and a poor person—their boast is the fear of the Lord.
It is not right to despise a wise poor person, and it is not right to honor a sinful person.
A leader, a judge, and a powerful person receive honor, but greater among them is the one who fears the Lord.
Free people will serve wise slaves, and a person of understanding does not grumble.
Do not act clever when doing your work, and do not glorify yourself in a time of hardship.
For it is better to work and have an abundance of everything than to glorify yourself while lacking bread.
My son, teach your soul gentleness and give it honor according to its worth.
Who will justify someone who sins against his own soul? And who will justify someone who despises his own life?
Someone honored in his wealth is in great poverty, and someone despised in his poverty is in great wealth.
The wisdom of a humble person will lift up his head and seat him among the great.
Do not honor a person because of his beauty, and do not despise a person because of his appearance.
For the bee is small among flying creatures, but its fruit is the finest of sweet things.
Do not boast about the clothes you wear, and do not exalt yourself on a day of glory, for the works of the Lord are wonders, and his works are hidden from human beings.
Many tyrants have sat on the ground, while someone whom no one expected has worn the crown.
Many powerful people have suffered great disgrace, and honored people have been handed over into the hands of others.
Do not find fault before you have investigated. Understand first, and then rebuke.
Do not speak before you have listened, and do not interrupt in the middle of a conversation.
Do not quarrel over a matter that is not yours, and do not join in the judgment of sinners.
My son, do not multiply your activities, for if they multiply, you will not escape sin. Even if you run, you will not catch up, and you will not escape by running.
There is someone who works hard, wears himself out, and hurries, yet suffers all the more loss.

There is someone who is weak and needs someone to support him, who lacks strength and is deeply impoverished. Yet the Lord's eye has looked down on him with kindness, and he has set him on his feet out of his humiliation.
He lifted his head, and many marveled at him.
Good things and evil, life and death, poverty and wealth come from the Lord.
What the Lord gives will remain among those who worship God, and his will shall stand firm forever.
There is someone who becomes rich through his [?] and the way he restrains himself, and this is his share of his reward.
When he says, “I have found rest; now I will eat from my good things,” he does not know what time will [?] upon him, when he will leave them to others and die.
Stand firm in your covenant, [?] in it, and grow old in your work.
Do not marvel at the works of a sinner. Instead, trust in the Lord and persist in your labors, for it is nothing for the Lord to make a poor person rich in an instant, suddenly.
The Lord's blessing is in the reward of the godly person, and very quickly he makes the blessing flourish.
Do not say, “What do I need from now on? And what good things will come to me from today onward?”
Do not say, “I have enough, and what trouble will overtake me from now on?”
For on a day of good things you do not remember the bad, and on a day of bad things you do not remember the good.
For it is nothing in the Lord's sight to repay a person according to his ways on the day of death.
The suffering of a single hour makes you forget luxury, and a person's deeds are revealed at his end.
Do not call anyone blessed before he dies, and a person is known through his children.
Do not bring just anyone into your house, for the deceitful person's traps are many.

For he turns good things into bad things and lays a trap for you, and he brings blame upon you for your wishes.

Do good to the humble person, and do not give to the ungodly. Set your bread aside, and do not give it to the ungodly, so that he cannot use it to overpower you. For you will receive twice as much evil for every good thing you do for him.
For the Most High himself hates sinners, and he will repay the ungodly with punishment.
Your friend will reveal himself to you in your prosperity, and your enemies will reveal themselves to you in your troubles.
A person's enemies grieve when he prospers, and his friend abandons him when he is in trouble.

So it is with someone who walks with a sinner and becomes entangled in his sins.

But they will make their creations last forever, and their prayer is in the practice of a craft. But the one who gives his soul leisure and meditates on the law of the Most High—
He will seek the wisdom of all the people of old and will not cease studying their prophecies.
He will preserve the counsel of famous people and will enter with them into the intricacies of parables.
He will seek the hidden meaning of proverbs and explore the riddles of parables.
He will serve among the great and appear before rulers. He travels through the lands of foreign nations, for he has tested the good and evil among people.
He will turn his heart first to the Lord who made him and plead before the Most High. He will open his mouth in prayer and plead for his sins.
If the great Lord wills, he will fill him with [?], and he will pour out [?] of his wisdom. He will give thanks to the Lord in prayer.
And he will set his counsel and teaching straight; he will reflect on his hidden mysteries.
He will reveal the teaching he has received, and he will take pride in the law of the Lord’s covenant.
Many will praise his wisdom, and it will never be erased. His memory will not cease, and his name will live from generation to generation.
The nations will tell of his wisdom, and an assembly will proclaim his honor.
If he lives on, he will leave a name greater than a thousand others; and if he dies, it will serve him well.
But I have reflected further, and I will speak; I am full like the moon.
Listen to me, my holy children, and blossom like a rose planted beside running water.
Give off your fragrance like frankincense, and blossom like a lily. Give off your scent and offer a blessing. Bless the Lord for all his works.
Magnify his name and proclaim his praise with songs from your lips and with lyres. Say this as you proclaim it:
“All the Lord’s works are very good, and every command will be fulfilled at its proper time.”

You must not say, “What is this, and what use is it?” For all these things will be examined at their proper time. At his word, the water stood like a heap of waterskins, and at the words of his mouth, there were storehouses of water.
All his will is contained in his command, and no one can hinder his salvation.
The deeds of every living person are before him, and they cannot be hidden from his eyes.
He has looked upon them from eternity to eternity, and nothing is extraordinary before him.
You must not say, “What is this, and what use is it?” For all things were created for their purpose.
His blessing overflowed like the river, and it watered the earth like a flood.
In this way his wrath will take possession of every nation, just as he turned waters into salt.
His paths are straight for the holy, but they are stumbling blocks for the lawless.
From the beginning he created good things for the good, and evil for sinners.
The basic necessities of human life are water, fire, iron, salt, wheat flour, milk, honey, the blood of grapes, oil, and clothing.
All these were created as good things for the godly; in the same way, they will be turned into evil things for sinners.
There are some that were created for vengeance, and in their anger they made their scourges strong. At the final time they will pour out their strength and appease the anger of the one who made them.
Fire, hail, famine, and death—all these were created for vengeance.
The teeth of wild beasts, scorpions, snakes, and the sword that takes vengeance to destroy the ungodly.
They will rejoice at his command and be ready in his hands upon the earth. At the appointed time they will not disobey a word.
For this reason I was resolved from the beginning; I reflected and put these things in writing.
For all the Lord’s works are good, and he will provide for every need at its proper time.
You cannot say, “This is worse than that,” for they are all good in their own time.
Now, then, bless him with your whole heart and with your mouth, and bless the Lord’s name.
Great toil has been created for everyone, and a heavy yoke rests on Adam’s children, from the day they come out of their mother’s womb until the day they are buried in the place of all people.
These are their anxieties and the fear in their hearts: thoughts of what they expect and of the day of their death.
From the person who sits in honor on a throne to the person brought low in earth and ashes,
from the person who wears purple and a crown down to the person dressed in a rough tunic,
there are anger, envy, turmoil, agitation, fear of death, worry, and strife. Even during the time of rest on their sleeping place, a dream at night disturbs their awareness.
His rest is brief, almost nothing. Even then, as though it were daytime, he anticipates dreams and is troubled by the vision in his heart, like someone who has escaped from a war.
He rises when he is safe, not astonished by any terror.
These are with all living creatures, from humans to animals, and seven times as much comes upon sinners.
Death, strife, bloodshed, the sword, traps, famine, destruction, and scourges.
All these were created for the lawless, and the flood happened because of them.
Everything that came from the earth will return to the earth, and what came from the waters will return to the sea.
Every gift and every act of oppression will disappear, but faithfulness will stand forever.
The wealth of oppressors will dry up like a river, and they will roar like loud thunder in a rainstorm.
When he opens his hands, they will rejoice. This is how transgressors will perish in the end.
The children of the ungodly will not spread their branches, and the roots of the unclean are like those on hard rocks.
The reed beside every body of water and on the riverbanks is pulled up before any grass.
Kindness is like a garden amid blessings, and mercy will last forever.
The life allotted to a laborer is good, but someone who has found a treasure is better off than he is.
Children and the building of a city establish a name, but a holy wife is better than both.
Wine and music gladden the heart, but love and wisdom are better than both.
A reed flute and a harp give joy, but a pleasant tongue is better than both.
Your eye will desire charm and beauty, but the green growth of the fields is better than both.
Your friend and your companion join you in your time, but a wife and her husband are better than both.
Brothers give you support and help in a time of trouble, but mercy will save you more than both.
Gold and silver establish a person, but counsel is better than both.
Wealth and power lift up the heart, but fear of the Lord is better than both. There is no lack in the fear of the Lord, and you do not need to seek help when you have it.
Fear of the Lord is like a garden of blessing, and it will shelter him more than anything else.
My son, do not live the life of a beggar, for it is better for you to die than to beg.
A man who looks to a table that is not his own has no life. He will defile his soul with food that is not his, but a wise and educated man will guard himself against this.
Begging will be sweet in the mouth of the shameless person, but a fire will blaze within him.
O death, how bitter the thought of you is to a person who is secure in his possessions, to a person who is free from worry and prospering in everything, and who is able to eat his food!
O death, how good your sentence is to a poor person who is weak and very old, who is troubled in everything, who has lost confidence and has given up endurance!
Do not be afraid of the sentence of death. Remember those who came before you and those who come after you,

for this is the decree for all flesh from the Lord. And what can you reject in the will of the Most High? Whether you live ten, a hundred, or a thousand years, there is no reproach concerning the length of life in the underworld.
The children of sinners will become desolate children, as will those who walk among the dwellings of the ungodly.
The inheritance of the children of sinners will perish, and reproach will remain with their descendants.
Children blame an ungodly father, because they will be reproached because of him.
Woe to you, ungodly people, who have abandoned the law of God Most High!
For if you are born, you will be born into a curse, and again, if you die, you will be assigned to a curse.
Everything that came from the earth will return to the earth. So it is with the ungodly: from a curse they go to destruction.
The mourning for people concerns their bodies, but the name of good people will not be erased.
Take care of your name, for it will remain with you longer than a thousand great treasures of gold.
It is a limited number of days [?], but a good name will last forever.
My children, keep the instruction in peace. Hidden wisdom and a treasure that is not revealed—what use are either of them?
A person who hides his foolishness is better than a person who hides his wisdom.
Therefore, be ashamed according to my words, for not every kind of shame is good, and not everything is desirable at all times for everyone.
Be ashamed before your father and your mother of sexual immorality, and before a great person and a ruler of lying,
and before a judge and an official of sin, and before an assembly and a people of lawlessness, and before a partner and a friend of wrongdoing,
and in the place where you lodge, of theft, and before the truth of God and the covenant, [?] at a place for eating, and of fickleness in receiving and giving.
And be ashamed of remaining silent before those who greet you, and of looking at a prostitute.
And of turning your face away from a relative, and of taking and giving, and of looking at a married woman.
And of scrutinizing his servant. Do not stand beside her bed. And be ashamed of reproaching friends with your words, and do not insult them after giving them something.

And be ashamed of repeating something you have heard, and of revealing secret matters. Then you will truly be modest and find favor before everyone. But do not be ashamed of these things, and do not show favoritism that leads you into sin:
Concerning the law of the Most High and the covenant, and a judgment that favors the ungodly.
Of a matter concerning a partner [?] companion; of giving your inheritance [?].
Of accuracy in weights and measures; of acquiring much or little;
Of trading, selling, and buying; of disciplining children severely; of making the sides of a wicked slave bleed.
A seal is good for a wicked woman, and lock things up where there are many hands.
Give whatever you give by number and measure, and put all receiving and giving in writing.
Of correcting a senseless person and a fool, and an old man being judged for sexual immorality. Then you will truly be well instructed and esteemed before every living person.

A daughter is a father's hidden night of watchfulness, and anxiety about her drives sleep away from him: while she is young, lest she grow too old; and when she has married, lest her husband hate her;
Lest she defile her virginity [?] in her parents' house; and when she has married, lest she transgress; and while she lives with her husband, lest she be barren.
Keep a very close watch over a stubborn daughter, lest she make your enemies rejoice over you and bring you shame before a great crowd.
Do not gaze at anyone's beauty, and do not gather among women.
For moths come out of clothes, and a woman's wickedness comes from a woman.
A man's wickedness is better than a woman who does good, and a woman who brings shame will become a stumbling block.
I will remember the Lord's works, and I will tell what I have seen. The Lord's works are through his words, and the blessing of his judgments has come into being.
The shining sun looks upon them all, and the Lord's work is full of his glory.
The Lord has not given the opportunity to the [?] his wonders, which the Lord Almighty [?] to establish everything in his glory.
He searched the abyss and the heart, and pondered it through his teachings. For the Lord knows every conscience, and he has looked upon a sign forever.
He tells what has passed and what will happen, and reveals the signs of hidden things.
For no thought has escaped him, and not a single word has been hidden from him.
He created the greatness of his wisdom. He exists before eternity and forever. He has not increased, nor does he diminish, and he has no need of any adviser.
How excellent all his works are! And what we see is [?] a spark.
All these things live and endure forever, and they all obey whenever needed.
They are all in pairs, one opposite another, and he has left nothing incomplete.
He has established each of his good things alongside another. And who can be satisfied with looking at his glory?
The splendor of the height, the purity of the firmament, [?] a glorious sight.
When the sun rises, appearing as it comes forth, it is a marvelous instrument, a work of the Most High.
At noon it scorches the lands, and who can stand before its burning heat?
A furnace is fanned for work, but the sun burns the mountains three times more fiercely than it, breathing out fiery flames. It dazzles the eyes as it spreads its rays.
Great is the Lord who made it, and at his words it hastens along its course.
And the moon, [?] in every activity of its appointed time, is the indicator of its seasons and an everlasting sign.
The sign of the festival comes from the moon, the giver of light that wanes at the end of its cycle.
The month is named after it. It is a marvel when it becomes full and changes, an instrument that represents the height, shining in the firmament of heaven.
The beauty of heaven is the glory of the stars. The Lord makes them shine in the heights.
At his words they will [?], and they do not slacken in their [?].
Look at the rainbow and bless the one who made it. It is very beautiful in its brightness.
It encircles heaven with its glorious arc. The hands of the Lord have completed it.
At his command he scatters the snow, and by his decree he sends out the lightning.
And the clouds came down like flying creatures; because of this the storehouses opened.
He strengthened the clouds of his greatness and scattered the hailstones.
The mountains will shake at his appearing, and the south wind will blow at his will.
(a) He made the earth tremble at the sound of his thunder. (b) And the north wind, with a gust of wind, scatters the snow like birds flying, and its descent is like locusts settling.
The eye is startled by the whiteness of its beauty; the heart marvels at its falling.
[?] the frost upon the earth like salt, and when it freezes it becomes like the points of thorns.
The north sends a cold wind. Ice freezes upon the waters, coming upon every gathering of water, and it clothes the water like armor.
It will devour the mountains, burn the desert, and consume the vegetation like fire.
Mist quickly heals all these things; dew refreshes them after the heat.
By his counsel he established the deep, and Jesus laid it waste.
Those who sail on the sea tell of its dangers, and we marvel at what we hear.
There are wonders there, and works of different colors, and every kind of living creature.
Order exists because of him, fulfillment belongs to him, and everything is established by his word.
We see many things, but we cannot reach him. And the sum of [?]: he is everything.
When we give him glory, what can we attain? For he is greater than all his works.
The Lord is awe-inspiring and exceedingly great, and his power is a wonder.
Exalt the Lord, giving him glory as much as you can, for he is far higher than that. Exert your strength as you exalt him. Do not grow weary, for you will not be able to reach him.
Who has seen him, so that he can speak about him? And who can exalt him as he truly is?
For we have seen only a few of his works, while many greater than these remain hidden.
The Lord himself made everything, and he gave wisdom to the godly.
Let us praise the honored men [?] honor.
God established a great glory of his greatness from eternity.
They exercised lordship in their kingdoms and were renowned for their power. They ruled through their wisdom and were spoken of among the prophets.
They led peoples through their counsels and were scribes of the people through their wisdom. Their teaching contained wise words.
They sought out musical [?] and expressed words in writing.
They were wealthy men, full of power, living peacefully in their homes.
All these received honor in their generations and became a source of pride in their days.
Some of them left their names behind so that their honors could be recounted.
Others among them have no remembrance. They perished as though they had never existed, and they became like those who had never been born, as did their children after them.
But these are merciful men whose righteous deeds were not forgotten.
It will remain with their [?]; the inheritance will be good [?].
Their descendants stood firm in the covenants.
Their descendants endure forever, and their glory will not be erased.
Their bodies were buried in peace, and their names live on for generations upon generations.
(b) And an assembly will recount their honor.
Enoch pleased the Lord, and he took him away as an example of repentance for the generations.
Noah was found perfectly righteous. He became a replacement in the time of wrath. For this reason the flood occurred; through him those who survived remained on the earth.
An everlasting covenant was established with him, so that all flesh would not be wiped out by a flood.
Abraham was the great father of many nations, and no one was found equal to him in glory.
He kept the law of the Most High. [?] a covenant with him; [?] covenant established in his flesh, and he was found faithful when tested.

Therefore he confirmed it to him with an oath: that the nations would be blessed through his descendants, that he would multiply him like the dust of the earth and establish his descendants like the stars, so that they would inherit from sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth.
He established it on these terms with Isaac because of Abraham his father.

The blessing of every person and the covenant rested on Jacob's head. He acknowledged him with his blessings and gave him an inheritance. He determined his portions and divided them among twelve tribes.
Moses was loved by God and by people, and his memory is blessed.
He made him equal in glory to the holy ones and exalted him through the terrors of his enemies.
He performed signs through his words. He gave him glory before the king, gave him commands before the people, and showed him his glory.
He purified him through faith and his gentleness. He chose him from among all flesh.
He let him hear his voice and brought him into the darkness. He gave him the commandments face to face, the law of life and instruction, to teach Jacob his covenant and Israel his judgments.
He exalted Aaron, his holy brother, who was like him, from the tribe of Levi.
He established his everlasting covenant with him and gave him the priesthood of the people. He blessed him with beautiful adornment and clothed him in a glorious robe.
He clothed him in complete splendor and equipped him with magnificent garments: trousers, a robe reaching to the feet, and an ephod.
He surrounded him with pomegranates and many golden bells, so that they would sound as he walked and their sound would be heard in the temple, as a reminder for the children of his people.
With a holy robe of gold and blue, and linen worked by an embroiderer, with a breastpiece of judgment for revealing the truth,

with spun scarlet worked by a craftsman, with precious stones engraved like seals in a gold setting made by a stone engraver, carved with writing as a reminder corresponding to the number of the tribes of Israel,
with a gold crown on top of the turban, bearing a seal of holiness: glorious honor, magnificent workmanship, beautiful and pleasing to the eyes.
There had never been anything like it before him, and no outsider will ever wear it, but only his sons and his sons’ sons forever.
They will offer their sacrifice in its entirety twice every day, continually.

Moses ordained him and anointed him with holy oil. It became an everlasting covenant for him and his descendants for as long as the heavens last, to serve him, to act as priests, and to bless his people in his name.
He chose him from among all people to offer incense and a sweet fragrance before the Lord as a memorial, to obtain forgiveness for your people.
He gave him his authoritative commandments in the covenant of judgment, to teach Jacob his testimonies and instruct Israel in his law.
For outsiders rose up against him, and Dathan and Abiram’s men were jealous of him in the wilderness, along with Korah’s assembly, in anger and rage.
The Lord saw and was displeased. He destroyed them in his furious anger. He performed wonders among them, [?] the fire of his flame.
He increased Aaron’s glory and gave him an inheritance of the firstfruits of the earliest crops. He allotted him the first bread, enough to satisfy him.
For they will eat the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave to him and his descendants.
But he will not inherit land belonging to the people, and he has no share among his people, for he is your share and your inheritance.

Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, was third in glory, because he was zealous in the fear of the Lord and stood firm when the people were angry, with the goodness and eagerness of his soul. He removed [?] from the people of Israel.
For this reason, a covenant of peace was established with him, to stand guard over his people's sanctuary, so that greatness and the priesthood would belong to him and his descendants forever.
And a covenant with the son David, from the tribe of Judah: an inheritance for the king's son through a single son, but the inheritance was for Aaron and his descendants.
May he give you wisdom in your hearts to judge his people with righteousness, so that their good things do not perish and their glory endures for ages upon ages.

Joshua, the son of Nun, was mighty in battle and succeeded Moses in prophecy. In keeping with his name, he became great in saving his chosen people, taking vengeance on the enemies who rose against them, so that he would give an inheritance to [?].
How glorious he was when he raised his hands and stretched out his sword against the cities!
Who ever stood before him like this? For the Lord brought him those who fought against him.
Was it not by his hand that the sun turned backward [?] day became two?
He called on the Lord of hosts, the Most High, when he was hard pressed by the enemies around him. The Lord answered him with hailstones of great force.

He brought them down in battle upon a nation and destroyed his opponents as they advanced, so that the nations would recognize their full armor and that his warfare was before the Lord. For he followed a mighty one.
And he showed mercy in the days of Moses. He and Caleb son of Jephunneh stood against them to keep the people from sin and to put an end to their wicked grumbling.
These two alone survived out of six hundred thousand foot soldiers, to bring them into their inheritance, into a land flowing with milk and honey.
The Lord gave Caleb strength, and it remained with him into his old age, so that they could climb to the heights. His descendants took possession of an inheritance.
This was so that all the children of Israel would see that it is good to follow the Lord.
And the judges, each one by name, whose hearts did not become unfaithful within them and who did not turn away from the Lord—may their memory be blessed.
May their bones flourish where they lie, and may they pass on their names to their honored children.
Samuel was loved by the Most High. He was the Lord's prophet; he established the kingship and anointed rulers over his people.
He judged the assembly according to the law of the Most High. The Lord watched over Jacob.
He chose him as a prophet because of his faithfulness, and through his visions he was recognized as faithful to him.
He called on the Lord of hosts when his enemies pressed him on every side, offering a lamb as a sacrifice.
The Lord thundered from heaven and made them hear his voice with a mighty sound.
He crushed the mighty tyrants and all the rulers of the Philistines.
And before he rested forever, he testified before the Lord and the king: "I have taken no money [?] from anyone, not even a sandal." And no one accused him.
And he prophesied after his death. He told the king of his death and raised his voice from the earth in a prophecy, wiping out the people's lawlessness.
After these things, Nathan arose and prophesied in the days of David.
Just as fat was set apart in a [?], so David was set apart from the sons of [?].
He played with lions as with a young goat, and with bears as with a lamb.
Did he not kill a giant in his youth and remove disgrace from the people by raising his hand with a sling stone to bring down Goliath’s arrogance?
He called upon the Lord Most High, and he gave strength to his right hand to destroy a mighty warrior in battle and to exalt the strength of his people.
Thus they honored him with tens of thousands upon tens of thousands, and they blessed him with the blessings of the Lord, bringing him a crown of glory.
For he crushed the enemies around him and destroyed the Philistines who opposed him. He crushed their strength to this day.
In all his deeds he gave thanks to the Holy Most High with words of glory. He praised him with his whole heart and loved the one who made him.
He stationed singers before the altar to sing praise to the sound of his voice.
He gave beauty to the festivals and adorned the appointed times completely, so that they would praise his holy name and the sanctuary would ring out from dawn.
The Lord forgave his sins and exalted his strength forever. He gave him the covenant of kings and a throne of glory in the [?].
His wise son arose after him and lived in prosperity because of him.
Solomon reigned in days of peace. God gave him rest on every side so that he could establish a house in his name and prepare the sanctuary forever.
How wise you were in your youth! You were filled with understanding like a river.
Your soul spread over the earth, and you were filled with riddling parables.
Your name reached the distant islands, and they loved your peace.
Through your songs, your proverbs, and your parables, countries marveled at you for your explanations.
In the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of [?], you gathered gold like tin and silver like lead.
You inclined your loins toward women, and they gained mastery over your bodies.
You stained your glory and defiled your descendants, bringing wrath upon your children and sorrow because of your foolishness.
So that the kingdom was divided, [?] from Ephraim ruled over a disobedient kingdom.

But the Lord will not abandon his mercy or cease his works. He will not wipe out the children of his chosen one or remove the descendants of the one he loved. He gave Jacob a remnant and David a root from him.

With his ancestors, he left behind one of his descendants, a fool among the people who lacked wisdom: Rehoboam, who divided the people through his counsel; and Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made [?] sin and set Ephraim on the path of sin.
Their sins multiplied greatly, so that they were driven out of their land.
He pursued every kind of wickedness until vengeance came down upon them.
Then Elijah the prophet arose like a fire, and his word burned like torches.
He was the one who brought famine upon them and humbled them in his zeal.
By the word of the Lord he shut up the sky and brought fire down upon them three times.
How you were honored, Elijah, through your wonders! Who is like you, that he may boast?
The one who raised a corpse from death and from the underworld by the word of the Most High.
The one who brought kings to destruction and brought the honored down from their beds.
The one who heard rebuke at Sinai and judgments of punishment at Horeb.
The one who anointed kings to carry out retribution and prophets to take his place after him.
The one who was taken up in a fiery whirlwind, in a chariot with fiery horses.
The one who was appointed to bring rebuke at the proper times, to calm wrath before anger broke out, to turn a father's heart toward his son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.
Blessed are those who saw you and those who fell asleep in love, for we too will surely live.
Elijah was covered by a whirlwind, and Elisha was filled with his spirit. No ruler shook him in his days, and no one took him by force.
No word prevailed over him, and his body prophesied when he was dead.
During his life he performed wonders, and his deeds were wonders even in his death.

Despite all these things, the people did not repent or turn away from their sins, until they were removed from the land and he scattered them over the whole earth. The people were left few in number, with no ruler in the house of David.
Some of them did his will, but others multiplied their sins.
Hezekiah strengthened his city and brought a water channel into its midst. He cut through the rock with iron and built springs to supply water.
In his days Sennacherib came up and sent the Rabshakeh. He went and raised his hand against Zion and acted insolently in his arrogance.
Then their hearts and their hands trembled, and they suffered pain like a woman about to give birth.
They cried out to the merciful Lord and stretched out their hands to him. The Holy One quickly heard them from heaven and saved them through Isaiah.
He struck the camp of the Assyrians, and his angel crushed them.
For Hezekiah did the Lord's will and was steadfast in the ways of David his father, which Isaiah the prophet commanded him to follow—Isaiah, who was great and trustworthy in his visions.
In his days the sun went backward, and he prolonged the king's life.
With a mighty spirit he saw the last things and comforted those who mourned in Zion.
He told them what would happen forever and revealed hidden things before they happened.
The memory of Josiah is like a blend of incense, prepared by the work of a perfume maker. It is sweet as honey in every mouth and like music at wine banquets.
He set the people's turning back on the right path and removed the abominations of lawlessness.
He directed his heart toward the Lord and strengthened devotion to God in the days of the lawless.
Except for David, Hezekiah, and Josiah, they all committed sin. For they abandoned the law of the Most High; the kings of Judah came to an end.
For they gave their power to others and their glory to a foreign nation.
For they burned the chosen city of their sanctuary and made its streets deserted.
Through Jeremiah—for they mistreated him, but he was consecrated as a prophet in the womb, to uproot, bring down, destroy, build, and plant.
Ezekiel, who saw the vision of glory that he showed him on the chariot of the cherubim.
For he also remembered the enemies in a storm, to do good to those who keep their ways straight.
May the bones of the twelve prophets blossom in their resting place. He encouraged Jacob and saved them through faith and hope.
How shall we exalt Zerubbabel? He was like a seal on the right hand.
And Joshua son of Jozadak: these men built the house in their days and raised up the Lord’s holy people, prepared for everlasting glory.
And furthermore, [?] greatly his memory—the memory of the one who raised our fallen walls, set up the gates and bars, and raised our houses.
No one was created on earth like Enoch, for he too was taken up from the earth.
No man was born like Joseph, greater than his brothers, a support for the people; and his bones received care.
Shem and Seth received honor among people, and Adam above every person in creation.
Simon son of Jeconiah, the high priest, renovated the house during his lifetime and strengthened the temple in his days.
Through him the foundations of the double height were laid, the top and the height of the temple enclosure.
In his days the water reservoirs burst; he increased the size of the bronze sea.
He took care of his people so that they would not fall, and he strengthened the city by building around it.
How honored he was among the people gathered around him when he came out from the house of the curtain!
He was like a morning star among the clouds, and like the moon, full of [?] in its days.
Like the sun shining upon the temple of the Most High, and like the rainbow shining in glorious clouds.
Like rose blossoms in the early days of the season, and like a lily beside flowing water; like a shoot of frankincense in the days of summer.
And like fire and frankincense in a censer, and like a vessel of hammered gold adorned with every precious stone.
And like an olive tree producing its fruit, like a cypress rising high among the clouds.
When he took a glorious robe and clothed himself in perfect splendor, when he went up to the holy altar, he brought glory to the court of the sanctuary.

When he received a portion from the hands of the priests, he stood beside the hearth of the censer, surrounded by a crown of his brothers. He was like a cedar shoot in Lebanon, and they surrounded him like the trunks of palm trees.
And all the sons of Aaron in their glory, with the Lord’s offering in their hands before the whole assembly of [?].
And the completion of the ministers’ service at the altars, adorning the offering of the Almighty Most High.
He stretched out his hand to the vessel for the drink offering and poured out the blood of the grape. He poured it at the foot of the altar as a fragrant offering to the Most High, the King of all.
Then Aaron’s sons shouted and sounded trumpets of beaten metal. They made a loud sound heard as a reminder before the Most High.
Then all the people hurried together and fell with their faces to the ground, worshiping the Lord Almighty, God Most High.
And the singers sang praises with their voices; [?] resounded in the great house.
And the people pleaded with the Lord Most High in their prayer before the Merciful One, until the adornment of the Lord was complete and they had finished his service.
Then he came down and raised his hands over the whole assembly of the children of [?], to give the Lord's blessing from their lips and to glory in his name.
(b) To receive the blessing from the Most High.
Now, then, bless the God of all, who does great things everywhere, who exalts our days from the womb, who deals with us according to his mercy.
May he give us gladness of heart, so that there may be peace in our days in [?], through days everlasting.
May [?] his mercy with us, and may he rescue us in his days.
My soul has hated two nations, and the third is not a nation.
The Philistines who live in Samaria, and the foolish people who live in Shechem.
I wrote the instruction in understanding and wisdom in this book—I, Jesus son of Sirach, Eleazar of Jerusalem, who poured forth wisdom from his heart.
Blessed is the person who walks in these things, and whoever puts them in his heart will become wise.
For if he does these things, he will prevail over them all, because his revelation is the light of the Lord.
I will praise you, Lord, my king. I will bless you, God, my Savior. I will praise your name.

For you became my helper and protector, and you saved my body from destruction, from fabricated slander by a tongue and from the lips of those who practice falsehood, and in the presence of those who stood against me.

And you brought deliverance according to the abundance of your mercy and your name. You rescued me from the mouth of the one ready to devour me, from the hands of those seeking my life, and from the many afflictions that overtook me.
And from the fury of a flame around me—I was not burned—from the midst of a fire.
And from the depths of Hades, from an unclean tongue and a lying word.
And from the slander of a king’s unjust tongue. My soul drew near to death, and my life was close to Hades below.
They seized me on every side, and there was no one to help me. I looked for someone to take me in, but I did not find him.
I remembered your name, Lord, and your work from eternity: that you have rescued those who wait patiently for you, and you save them from the hands of their enemies.
He lifted my servitude up from the earth, and I pleaded to be rescued from death.
I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, not to abandon me in the days of affliction, in a time of arrogance when there was no help.
I will bless your name at all times, and I will praise you openly, because you heard my plea.
For you saved me from destruction and rescued me from an evil time. Therefore I will acknowledge you, praise you, and bless your name, Lord.
While I was still young, before I traveled, I sought wisdom before my prayer.
And I prayed for her before the temple, and I will seek her until the end.
I blossomed like a vine that had spread out. My heart rejoiced in her. My foot stood on the straight path; I sought her from my youth.
I inclined my ear a little and received her, and through her I found much instruction for myself.
Through her I was raised up. I will give glory to the one who gives me wisdom.
For I resolved to practice it. I was zealous for what is good, and I will not be ashamed.
My soul struggled for her, and I strove for her in hunger. I spread out my hands toward heaven and mourned my acts of ignorance concerning her.
I directed my soul toward her and found her in purity. From the beginning I gained understanding in her company; therefore he will not abandon me.
And my heart was troubled as I searched for her. Therefore I acquired a good possession for myself.
The Lord gave me a tongue as a reward. With it I will bless him.
Come to me, you who lack instruction, and live in the house of instruction.
Why are you in need, when you are going to speak about these things, and your souls are so thirsty?
I opened my mouth and spoke: "Acquire it for yourselves free of charge."
Put your neck under her yoke, and let your soul receive instruction, for she is close at hand.
See with your own eyes that I labored a little and found great rest for myself.
Acquire instruction for yourselves with a large sum of copper money, and you will gain much time through it.
Let your soul rejoice in his mercy, and may you not be ashamed of his blessing.
Do your work ahead of time, and he will give you your reward at the appointed time. The Wisdom of Jesus son of Sirach.
